rules.why: The buyer pays cash out of a €200,000 budget, and taxes and fees add roughly 3.5-8% on top of the price depending on the country, so a price cap of €185,000 keeps the total cost inside budget everywhere.
The plan asks for a small flat with one or two bedrooms, so studios and larger family homes are left out.

After agency fees, empty months, upkeep, rent tax and buying costs are subtracted, the flat must still earn at least 6.5% a year - a demanding bar that only the best handful of listings clear, which is what earning the most means here.

A flat priced below 70% of its neighbourhood's usual price per m² is usually cheap because it needs big repairs, the buyer's stated worst case, so the most suspicious bargains are dropped while fair deals stay.

Because tenants are long-term locals found through an agency, the flat should sit in a neighbourhood with a working rental market (around 20 or more rental listings) so it does not stand empty for months.
The buyer holds for ten years and wants prices rising, so only countries where house prices rose at least about 3% last year are kept; all three candidate countries currently pass this.
The search stays inside the three chosen cities, all within three hours' flight of Amsterdam and open to a Dutch buyer without any permit.

With a €200,000 cash budget and 3.5-8% in taxes and fees added on top of the price depending on the country, a €185,000 price cap keeps the total purchase inside budget everywhere, so this rule stays unchanged.
The plan asks for a small flat with one or two bedrooms, so studios and larger family homes are left out.

The after-costs return floor drops from 6.5% to 6% because 6.5% sat above almost every fairly-priced flat outside Lodz, while 6% still clearly beats the 3-5.5% a typical flat nets in these cities and lets Bari's stronger neighbourhoods qualify so the buyer can compare two countries.

Kept at 0.7 because it is doing its job: it excluded the €5,000-17,000 Bari listings with impossible 19-123% 'yields' that are almost certainly wrecks or junk, which is exactly the big-repairs worst case the buyer wants flagged.
Kept at 20 or more rental listings per neighbourhood, since an agency needs an active local rental market to find long-term tenants quickly, and all Lodz zones plus Bari's main zones pass.
Kept: only countries where house prices rose at least about 3% over the last year are allowed, and all three candidate countries currently pass.
Kept: the search stays inside the three chosen cities, all within three hours' flight of Amsterdam and open to a Dutch buyer without any permit.

The only change this round: v2 found 70 matches, just over the 60 ceiling, so the after-costs return floor rises slightly from 6.0% to 6.2%; this trims the weakest tail while keeping both cities, since fairly-priced Bari flats net in the low 6s and Lodz's best reach about 7%.
